accurately

(adverb). in a way that is correct and true in every detail; exactly

ex: The plans should be drawn as accurately as possible

turret

(noun). A small tower on top of a larger tower or at the corner of a building or wall, typically of a castle.

ex: a small tower on top of a larger tower or at the corner of a building or wall, typically of a castle.

stable

(noun). a building set apart and adapted for keeping horses.

ex: If the foundations of the house aren't stable, collapse is possible.

revolutionary

(adjective). connected with political revolution

ex: He was arrested for taking part in revolutionary activities.

competitor

(noun). a person who takes part in an athletic contest

ex: How many competitors took part in the race?

principal

(adjective). First in order of importance; main. >< secondary, minor

ex: He was principal dancer at the Dance Theatre of Harlem.

contestant

(noun). a person who takes part in a contest or competition

ex: In tonight's quiz, our contestants have come from all over the country.

mathematician

(noun). a person who is an expert in mathematics

ex: She is one of the world's foremost theoretical mathematicians

instrument

(noun). a tool or device used for a particular task, especially for delicate or scientific work

ex: They're surgical instruments

adopt

(verb). Take on or assume (an attitude or position)

ex: I think it's time to adopt a different strategy in my dealings with him.

horizon

(noun). The line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet

ex: We could see a row of camels silhouetted on the horizon.

modern

(adjective). of the present time or recent times

ex: My grandpa's attitudes are very modern, considering his age.

figure

(noun). a person of a particular kind, especially one who is important or distinctive in some way

ex: The unemployment rate is now in double figures.

ultimate

(adjective). happening at the end of a long process

ex: My manager will make the ultimate decision about who to employ.

escapement

(noun). A mechanism in a clock or watch

ex: the time in which the escapement or connexion is being completed.

detent

(noun). A catch in a machine which prevents motion until released

ex: a system of detents is used to ensure that gears are held in whatever position is selected

coordinate

(verb). to organize different parts of an activity and people involved in it so that it works well

ex: We need someone to coordinate the whole campaign.

inconvenience

(noun). Trouble or difficulty caused to one's personal requirements or comfort.

ex: We apologize for any inconvenience caused by the late arrival of the train.

fluctuating

(adjective). Rising and falling irregularly in number or amount.

ex: Using temporary workers helps firms to cope with fluctuating demand.

attempt

(noun). an effort to achieve or complete a difficult task or action.

ex: He attempted a joke, but no one laughed.

tremendous

(adjective). Very great in amount, scale, or intensity.

ex: They were making a tremendous amount of noise last night.

alternate

(verb). Occur in turn repeatedly.

ex: She alternated between cheerfulness and deep despair.

adequately

(adverb). in a way that is enough in quantity

ex: Manufacturers may lack the means to adequately test their product.

sections.title: Passage 2: The Evolutionary Mystery- Crocodile Survives
sections.html:
historical

(adjective). Of or concerning history or past events.

ex: She specializes in historical novels set in 18th-century England.

supreme

(adjective). (of authority or an office, or someone holding it) superior to all others.

ex: the supreme commander of the armed forces

survivor

(noun). a person who survives, especially a person remaining alive after an event in which others have died

ex: She's a cancer survivor/a survivor of cancer.

crocodile

(noun). A large predatory semiaquatic reptile with long jaws, long tail, short legs, and a horny textured skin.

ex: He lost an arm to a crocodile.

primitive

(adjective). belonging to a very simple society with no industry

ex: The spiny anteater is a mammal, although a very primitive one.

ancestor

(noun). a person, typically one more remote than a grandparent

ex: There were portraits of his ancestors on the walls of the room.

adapt

(verb). Make (something) suitable for a new use or purpose

ex: We had to adapt our plans to fit Jack's timetable.

lifestyle

(noun). the way in which a person lives.

ex: She needs a pretty high income to support her lifestyle.

contemporary

(adjective). Living or occurring at the same time

ex: Although the play was written hundreds of years ago, it still has a contemporary (= modern) feel to it.

reptile

(noun). a vertebrate animal of a class that includes snakes, lizards,

ex: Humans, insects, reptiles, birds and mammals are all animals.

extinct

(adjective). (of a species, family, or other larger group) having no living members

ex: There is concern that the giant panda will soon become extinct.

climate

(noun). The weather conditions prevailing in an area in general or over a long period.

ex: When we retire, we're going to move to a warmer climate.

witness

(verb). see (an event, typically a crime or accident) take place

ex: Police are appealing for witnesses to the accident to come forward.

dinosaur

(noun). a fossil reptile of the Mesozoic era, in many species reaching an enormous size

ex: This computer's a dinosaur, isn't it?

planet

(noun). A celestial body moving

ex: Might there be intelligent life on other planets?

alleged

(adjective). stated as a fact but without any proof

ex: They were in the house when the alleged crime took place.

mammalian

(adjective). Relating to or denoting a mammal.

ex: He is an expert on mammalian extinctions.

dominance

(noun). Power and influence over others.

ex: the company's growing dominance of the sports shoe industry

alligator

(noun). A large semiaquatic reptile similar to a crocodile but with a broader and shorter head, native to the Americas and China

ex: There are sharks in the water, alligators on the island, and a hidden explosive in the boat.

prehistoric

(adjective). relating to or denoting the period before written records.

ex: Painting originated in prehistoric times.

incredibly

(adverb). To a great degree; extremely.

ex: Incredibly, no one was hurt in the accident.

adaptive

(adjective). concerned with changing; able to change when necessary in order to deal with different situations

ex: These governments do not possess the adaptive capacity to endure such changes.

roamer

(noun). someone who likes to move around and travel, especially without a clear idea of what they want to do

ex: He's a bit of a roamer, so he could be anywhere in the country.

existence

(noun). The fact or state of living or having objective reality.

ex: Many people question the existence of God.

approximately

(adverb). almost, but not completely

ex: The job will take approximately three weeks, and cost approximately £1,000.

feature

(noun). a distinctive attribute or aspect of something.

ex: Our latest model of phone has several new features.

stealth

(noun). Cautious and surreptitious action or movement.

ex: She moved across the field with the stealth of a cat on the prowl.

streamline

(verb). design or provide with a form that presents very little resistance to a flow of air or water, increasing speed and ease of movement

ex: The bodies of dolphins are more streamlined than those of porpoises.

streamlined

(adjective). having a streamlined shape.

ex: Our latest model has been revamped to give it a more modern, streamlined look.

tail

(noun). a thing resembling an animal's tail in its shape or position, typically something extending downward or outward at the end of something.

ex: The dog wagged its tail excitedly.

armour

(noun). the metal coverings formerly worn by soldiers or warriors

ex: Police put on body armour before confronting the rioters.

jaw

(noun). each of the upper and lower bony structures in vertebrates forming the framework of the mouth and containing the teeth

ex: He has a strong/square jaw.

webbed

(adjective). having the toes connected by a membrane

ex: Those are webbed toes/feet

capacity

(noun). A specified role or position

ex: The generators each have a capacity of (= can produce) 1,000 kilowatts.

underestimate

(verb). to not realize how good, strong, determined, etc. somebody really is

ex: Don't underestimate the difficulties of getting both parties to the conference table.

especially

(adverb). more in particular circumstances than in others

ex: She's not especially interested in sport.

metabolism

(noun). The chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life.

ex: Exercise is supposed to speed up your metabolism.

unique

(adjective). being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.

ex: I'd recognize your handwriting anywhere - it's unique.

coldblooded

(adjective). (of a kind of animal) having a body temperature varying with that of the environment; poikilothermic.

ex: Cold-blooded animals depend on the temperature of their immediate environment.

surrounding

(adjective). All round a particular place or thing.

ex: The shop draws customers from many surrounding areas.

consequently

(adverb). As a result.

ex: All the shops were closed, and consequently we couldn't buy any food.

exposure

(noun). The state of being exposed to contact with something.

ex: You should always limit your exposure to the sun.

sunlight

(noun). light from the sun

ex: The lake sparkled in the bright sunlight.

vulnerable

(adjective). Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally

ex: I felt very vulnerable, standing there without any clothes on.

shortage

(noun). A state or situation in which something needed cannot be obtained i

ex: The long hot summer has led to serious water shortages.

survive

(verb). remain alive

ex: These plants cannot survive in very cold conditions.

outlive

(verb). (of a person) live longer than (another person).

ex: women generally outlive men

volatile

(adjective). liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse.

ex: Food and fuel prices are very volatile in a war situation.

intake

(noun). an amount of food, air, or another substance taken into the body

ex: I heard a sharp intake of breath behind me.

efficient

(adjective). effective with the least energy/manpower consumed

ex: The city's transport system is one of the most efficient in Europe.

prey

(noun). An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

ex: A hawk hovered in the air before swooping on its prey.

vibration

(noun). An instance of vibrating

ex: Aircraft manufacturers want to reduce vibration for the sake of safety.

switch

(verb). change the position, direction of something

ex: she's managed to switch careers

snatch

(verb). Quickly seize (something) in a rude or eager way.

ex: She had her purse snatched (= stolen) while she was shopping.

waterside

(noun). the edge of or area adjoining a sea, lake, or river.

ex: it was built on the waterside

anticipation

(noun). The action of anticipating something; expectation or prediction

ex: She's even decorated the spare room in anticipation of your visit.

gazelle

(noun). a small slender antelope that typically has curved horns and a yellowish-brown coat with white underparts

ex: Gazelle companies expand at double-digit rates.

ambush

(noun). surprise attack on (someone) from a concealed position

ex: Several passers-by were killed in the ambush.

drown

(verb). to die because you have been underwater too long and you cannot breathe; to kill somebody in this way

ex: He drowned in a boating accident.

favorable

(adjective). Expressing approval.

ex: The movie received generally favorable reviews.

impact

(verb). contact strongly with another object

ex: The bullet explodes on impact (= when it hits another object).

drought

(noun). A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall

ex: This year (a) severe drought has ruined the crops.

habitat

(noun). The natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism.

ex: Secondly, the wildlife has to compete with the surrounding agriculture for the habitat.

regulate

(verb). Control or maintain the rate or speed of (a machine or process) so that it operates properly.

ex: Her mother strictly regulates how much TV she can watch.

mud

(noun). wet earth that is soft and sticky

ex: The vehicles got bogged down in the heavy mud.

transform

(verb). Make a marked change in the form, nature, or appearance of.

ex: The reorganization will transform the entertainment industry.

quiescent

(adjective). in a state or period of inactivity or dormancy.

ex: The political situation was now relatively quiescent.

aestivation

(noun). Prolonged torpor or dormancy of an insect, fish, or amphibian during a hot or dry period.

ex: Entry of adults into aestivation followed the same pattern but began two months after diapause started.

mechanism

(noun). A natural or established process by which something takes place

ex: These automatic cameras have a special focusing mechanism.

detect

(verb). Discover or identify the presence or existence of.

ex: Some sounds cannot be detected by the human ear.

metabolic

(adjective). Relating to or deriving from the metabolism of a living organism.

ex: The athletes had taken pills to stimulate their metabolic rate

flux

(noun). The action or process of flowing

ex: Our plans are in a state of flux at the moment

plasma

(noun). The colourless fluid part of blood, lymph, or milk, in which corpuscles or fat globules are suspended.

ex: When high power laser radiation interacts with the surface of the target, a hot plasma layer is formed.

fluid

(noun). A substance that has no fixed shape and yields easily to external pressure;

ex: If you have a fever you should drink plenty of fluids.

sample

(noun). A small part or quantity intended to show what the whole is like.

ex: Please bring some samples of your work to the interview.

accumulation

(noun). The acquisition or gradual gathering of something.

ex: Accumulations of sand can be formed by the action of waves on coastal beaches.

nitrogenous

(adjective). Containing nitrogen in chemical combination.

ex: They're nitrogenous fertilizers

electrolyte

(noun). a liquid or gel that contains ions and can be decomposed by electrolysis, e.g., that present in a battery.

ex: Electrolyte balance is related to hydration, making fluid intake extremely important

concentration

(noun). The relative amount of a particular substance contained within a solution or mixture

ex: High concentrations of toxic elements were found in the polluted areas.

function

(verb). work or operate in a proper or particular way.

ex: The function of the veins is to carry blood to the heart.

urine

(noun). a watery, typically yellowish fluid stored in the bladder and discharged through the urethra. It is one of the body's chief means of eliminating excess water and salt

ex: Can you provide a urine sample?

reserve

(noun). a supply of a commodity not needed for immediate use but available if required

ex: she trusted him without reserve

fluctuate

(verb). rise and fall irregularly in number or amount.

ex: trade with other countries tends to fluctuate from year to year

proportional

(adjective). Corresponding in size or amount to something else.

ex: the punishment should be proportional to the crime

emerge

(verb). move out of way and become visible

ex: the economy has started to emerge from recession

dehydration

(noun). the loss or removal of water from something

ex: Diarrhoea and vomiting lead to dehydration unless fluids are taken to replace the loss.

reckon

(verb). be of the opinion.

ex: I reckon it's going to rain.

harsh

(adjective). cruel, severe and unkind

ex: The children had had a harsh upbringing.

starvation

(noun). Suffering or death caused by lack of food.

ex: The animals had died of starvation.

survival

(noun). the act or fact of living or continuing longer than another person or thing

ex: The doctors told my wife I had a 50/50 chance of survival.

throughout

(adverb). during a whole period of time.

ex: People throughout the country are out of work.

scheme

(noun). A large-scale systematic plan or arrangement for attaining some particular object

ex: Under the current marking/mark scheme, you need 90 percent to get an A.

evolve

(verb). develop gradually and in distinct stages

ex: Did humans evolve from apes?

freshwater

(adjective). of or found in fresh water; not of the sea

ex: The village is near a freshwater pond.

resource

(noun). A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets

ex: The country's greatest resource is the dedication of its workers.

access

(noun). the means or opportunity to approach or enter a place

ex: The main access to (= entrance to) the building is at the side.

tough

(adjective). (of a person) strong and prone to violence

ex: Children's shoes need to be tough.

display

(verb). Put (something) in a prominent place

ex: Family photographs were displayed on the wall.

retain

(verb). Continue to have (something); keep possession of.

ex: She succeeded in retaining her lead in the second half of the race.

proportionately

(adverb). In a way that corresponds in size or amount to something else.

ex: The importance and influence of the diet increased proportionately.

aestivate

(verb). To be in a dormant or torpid state during a hot dry period, such as the summer months.

ex: The toads must aestivate during the summer, burrowing down into the soil to survive the heat.

sections.title: Passage 3: Company Innovation
sections.html:
safeguard

(noun). A measure taken to protect someone

ex: The disk has built-in safeguards to prevent certain errors.

innovative

(adjective). featuring new methods; advanced and original

ex: She was an imaginative and innovative manager.

license

(noun). a permit of authority to do something

ex: She has a fishing/export/driver’s license

intellectual

(adjective). well educated and connected with logical processes

ex: I like detective stories and romances - nothing too intellectual.

property

(noun). A thing or things belonging to someone; possessions collectively.

ex: Both books have "Government property" stamped inside them.

integrate

(verb). Combine (one thing) with another to form a whole.

ex: Children are often very good at integrating into a new culture.

confront

(verb). Come face to face with argumentative intent.

ex: As she left the court, she was confronted by angry crowds who tried to block her way.

jeopardise

(verb). to risk harming or destroying something/somebody

ex: a devaluation of the dollar would jeopardize New York's position as a financial center

innovation

(noun). the introduction of new things, ideas

ex: The recording industry is driven by constant innovation.

concept

(noun). An abstract idea

ex: The concept of free speech is unknown to them.

reshape

(verb). to change the shape or structure of something

ex: Baby boomers continue to reshape society as they age.

industry

(noun). Economic activity concerned with the processing of raw materials

ex: The city needs to attract more industry.

switch

(verb). change the position, direction of something

ex: She started studying English, but switched to History in her second year.

entire

(adjective). With no part left out; whole.

ex: Between them they ate an entire cake.

financial

(adjective). relating to finance

ex: Is there any hope of getting financial support for the project?

resolve

(verb). Settle or find a solution to (a problem or contentious matter)

ex: Have you resolved the problem of transport yet?

venture

(noun). A risky or daring journey or undertaking.

ex: She advised us to look abroad for more lucrative business ventures.

capital

(noun). the city or town that functions as the seat of government

ex: London used to be the financial capital of the world.

commercialize

(verb). Manage or exploit in a way designed to make a profit

ex: How can this technology be commercialized?

field

(noun). a particular branch of study or sphere of activity or interest

ex: we talked to professionals in various fields

intimidate

(verb). frighten

ex: They were intimidated into accepting a pay cut by the threat of losing their jobs.

predict

(verb). Say or estimate that (a specified thing) will happen in the future

ex: It's still not possible to accurately predict the occurrence of earthquakes.

goods

(noun). things that are produced to be sold

ex: They sell leather goods such as wallets, purses, and briefcases.

brilliant

(adjective). Exceptionally clever or talented.

ex: Her mother was a brilliant scientist.

scientist

(noun). a person who is studying or has expert knowledge of one or more of the natural or physical sciences

ex: Her mother was a brilliant scientist.

incomprehension

(noun). failure to understand something.

ex: She stared at him in total incomprehension.

lab

(noun). a laboratory.

ex: She works in a chemistry lab.

shabby

(adjective). in poor condition through long or hard use or lack of care

ex: He wore a shabby old overcoat.

downtown

(adverb). in or to the central part of a city

ex: I work downtown, but I live in the suburbs.

AI

(noun). artificial intelligence

ex: Artificial intelligence research has been going on for decades

programmer

(noun). a person who writes computer programs.

ex: He used to work as a computer programmer for a software company.

mimic

(verb). Imitate (someone or their actions or words)

ex: She was mimicking the various people in our office

sexologist

(noun). a scientist who studies human sexual behaviour

ex: His career as a sexologist (now the subject of a film, which opens next month) began in 1938

dietitian

(noun). An expert on diet and nutrition.

ex: we have a team of dieticians to ensure patients get healthy, balanced meals

coach

(noun). an athletic instructor or trainer.

ex: Gus Poyet was appointed as head coach.

specialist

(noun). having or involving expert knowledge of a particular area of work, study or medicine

ex: She's a specialist in modern French literature

client

(noun). A person or organization using the services of a lawyer

ex: Mr Black has been a client of this firm for many years.

seek

(verb). Attempt to find (something)

ex: "Are you actively seeking jobs?" she asked.

virtual

(adjective). almost or very nearly the thing described

ex: He is a virtual prisoner in his own home.

objective

(noun). a thing aimed at or sought; a goa

ex: Can the sales team achieve/meet its financial objectives?

expert

(noun). A person who is knowledgeable about or skilful in a particular area

ex: My mother is an expert at dress-making (= she does it very well).

statistics

(noun). the practice or science of collecting and analysing numerical data in large quantities

ex: The statistics show that, in general, women live longer than men.

intangible

(adjective). Unable to be touched; not having physical presence

ex: She has that intangible quality which you might call charisma.

terrify

(verb). cause to feel extreme fear

ex: The idea of parachuting out of a plane terrifies me.

evident

(adjective). clear; easily seen

ex: The full extent of the damage only became evident the following morning.

globally

(adverb). in a way that relates to the whole world

ex: The company has to be able to compete globally.

desperate

(adjective). Feeling or showing a hopeless sense that a situation is so bad as to be impossible to deal with.

ex: The situation is desperate - we have no food, very little water and no medical supplies.

hormone

(noun). any of various chemicals made by living cells that influence the development, growth, sex, etc. of an animal

ex: All right, men are hormone driven fools.

merger

(noun). a combination of two things, especially companies, into one

ex: She's an attorney who advises companies about mergers and takeovers.

empire

(noun). An extensive group of states or countries ruled over by a single monarch

ex: It used to be said that Britain ruled an empire on which the sun would never set.

creativity

(noun). The use of imagination or original ideas to create something;

ex: Too many rules might deaden creativity.

disregard

(verb). Pay no attention to

ex: Even as he spoke the words, he knew he'd never disregard his friend

corporation

(noun). a company or group of people authorized to act as a single entity and recognized as such in law.

ex: She didn't want to work for a big corporation where everything was so impersonal.

management

(noun). the act of running and controlling a business

ex: There is a need for stricter financial management.

risk

(noun). a situation involving exposure to danger

ex: There's a high risk of another accident happening in this fog.

accidental

(adjective). Happening by chance, unintentionally, or unexpectedly

ex: The site was located after the accidental discovery of bones in a field.

straightforward

(adjective). easy to do or to understand

ex: Just follow the signs to Bradford - it's very straightforward.

attitude

(noun). A settled way of thinking or feeling about something

ex: It's often very difficult to change people's attitudes.

pessimistic

(adjective). Tending to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen.

ex: The tone of the meeting was very pessimistic.

prosper

(verb). grow or develop in a healthy way.

ex: Lots of microchip manufacturing companies prospered at that time.

intensive

(adjective). Concentrated on a single subject or into a short time

ex: Intensive bombing had reduced the city to rubble.

pharmaceutical

(adjective). relating to medicinal drugs, or their preparation, use, or sale

ex: The British pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca employs about 5,000 people in the town

entrepreneur

(noun). A person who sets up a business or businesses

ex: He was one of the entrepreneurs of the 80s who made their money in property.

costly

(adjective). costing a lot; expensive

ex: The project was subject to several costly delays/setbacks.

clinical

(adjective). relating to the observation and treatment of actual patients rather than theoretical or laboratory studies

ex: Clinical trials of the new drug may take five years.

enterprise

(noun). A project or undertaking, especially a bold or complex one

ex: Don't forget this is a commercial enterprise - we're here to make money.

impressive

(adjective). Evoking admiration through size, quality, or skill;

ex: That was an impressive performance from such a young tennis player.

triumphant

(adjective). Having won a battle or contest

ex: She made a triumphant return to the stage after several years of working in television.

incorporate

(verb). combine

ex: This aircraft incorporates several new safety features.

restructure

(verb). to organize something such as a system or a company in a new and different way

ex: The government restructured the coal industry before selling it to private owners.

sufficient

(adjective). Enough; adequate.

ex: This recipe should be sufficient for five people.

disruptive

(adjective). causing problems, noise, etc. so that something cannot continue normally

ex: His teacher described him as a noisy, disruptive influence in class.

proposal

(noun). a formal suggestion or plan; the act of making a suggestion

ex: I didn't put forward any such proposal

glee

(noun). great delight.

ex: his face lit up with impish glee

recall

(verb). (not used in the progressive tenses) to remember something

ex: I can still vaguely recall being taken to the hospital
